title: Electric Charges and Fields: Chapter Introduction
summary: A rubbed comb lifts paper bits without touching them. Rubbing moves electrons, a charged body attracts even neutral paper by induction, and every charge reaches out through its electric field.

notes.title: 00 – Electric Charges and Fields: Chapter Introduction

keyPoints: Rubbing transfers **electrons**: a plastic comb run through dry hair gains electrons and becomes **negative**.
Two kinds of charge: **like charges repel, unlike charges attract**.
A charged body attracts a **neutral** one by **induction**: the nearer opposite charge wins.
**Coulomb's law** F = kq₁q₂/r²: double the distance and the force becomes one-fourth. Each charge sets up an **electric field**; field lines start on + and end on −.

list: Rubbing moves electrons from the hair to the comb: the comb becomes negatively charged, the hair positively.
The paper is neutral, but near the comb its charges shift slightly: positive charge nearer the comb, negative charge farther away.
The nearer (attractive) charge feels a stronger force than the farther (repulsive) one, so the net force pulls the paper to the comb. This is **induction**.

blocks.formula: F = k q₁q₂ / r²,   k = 1/(4πε₀) ≈ 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²

blocks.p: A charge q sets up an **electric field** E around it; another charge q₀ placed there feels F = q₀E. The field is how a force acts without contact.

list: Field lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges.
The tangent to a field line gives the direction of E; closer lines mean a stronger field.
Electric charge, conductors and insulators, charging by induction, basic properties of charge.
Coulomb's law and forces between multiple charges.
Electric field, field lines, electric dipole.
Electric flux and Gauss's law, with its applications.

quiz.q: A plastic comb run through dry hair becomes:
quiz.explain: Electrons move from the hair to the comb.

quiz.q: A charged comb attracts neutral paper because of:
quiz.explain: Charges in the paper shift; the nearer opposite charge wins.

quiz.q: If the distance between two charges is doubled, the force becomes:

options: Start on negative and end on positive charges
Start on positive and end on negative charges
Form closed loops around a charge
quiz.explain: They begin on + and end on −, and never cross.
